'''Christine Bycroft''' is a [[New Zealand]] [[statistician]] and [[demographer]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Christine Bycroft's research |url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Christine-Bycroft-2087405840 |access-date=2 August 2023}}</ref> 

==Biography==
Bycroft is a principal population statistician at [[Statistics New Zealand]], for whom she has published an analysis comparing the costs and benefits of running a full census or alternatively using a system of administrative data registers modeled after similar systems in the [[Nordic countries]].{{r|dtcm}}

From 2005 to 2006, Bycroft took a year away from Statistics New Zealand to work for the U.K. [[Office for National Statistics]].{{r|away}} She was promoted to Senior Research Statistician at Statistics New Zealand in 2008.{{r|promo}}

Bycroft is an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]]{{r|isimem}} she was elected to the Institute in 2010.{{r|elected}} She represents New Zealand and is one of three representatives for [[Oceania]] in the Committee on Women in Statistics of the International Statistical Institute.{{r|c4w}}
She also served on the council of the International Association of Survey Statisticians from 2011 to 2015,{{r|iass}}
and on the council of the Population Association of New Zealand until 2014.{{r|panz}}
